chunks: From him, from a group of our scholars, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Naeem al-Qabusi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) that he said:

My son Ali, the eldest of my children, is the one most preferred by me and the one most loved by me. He examined the leather case (Jafr) with me. Only a prophet or the testamentary trustee (Wasi) of a prophet can examine it.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, the 7th Imam
key_terms.أَثَرُهُمْ: The most preferred or chosen among them
key_terms.الْجَفْر: The sacred leather case containing divine knowledge and the rights of the Imams
key_terms.الْوَصِيّ: The testamentary trustee or designated successor of a Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who is the testamentary trustee (Wasi) capable of examining the Jafr alongside the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim explicitly identifies Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha as his eldest and most beloved son, grounding this affection in his unique spiritual authority. The Imam highlights that Ali shared in the contemplation of the *Jafr*, a sacred repository of divine knowledge, a privilege exclusive to Prophets and their *Wasi* (successors), thereby affirming the continuity of the Imamate. This designation serves as a crucial link in the chain of succession, emphasizing the hereditary and divinely appointed nature of the Imams in Shia tradition.
